lede: Quraysh asked why the Qurʾan had not been sent down to a great man of one of the two towns. This surah answers by saying what wealth is worth to Allah: were it not that all people would become one in disbelief, He would have given those who reject Him houses with roofs of silver — and ornaments of gold.

names.name: al-Zukhruf
names.note: From its thirty-fifth ayah. Zukhruf is gold, and anything gilded or adorned. It is also called Ḥā Mīm al-Zukhruf: the fourth of the seven Ḥā Mīm surahs.

revelation.detail: It is Makkan by agreement, as Ibn al-Jawzī and al-Qurṭubī both record. Muqātil excepted a single ayah, the forty-fifth. The traditional order places it sixty-third.

evidence.quote: سُورَةُ الزُّخْرُفِ هِيَ مَكِّيَّةٌ بِإجْماعِهِمْ وَقالَ مُقاتِلٌ: هي مَكِّيَّةٌ، إلّا آيَةً

attested.quote: أخْرَجَ ابْنُ مَرْدُويَهْ عَنِ ابْنِ عَبّاسٍ قالَ: نَزَلَتْ بِمَكَّةَ سُورَةُ (حم الزُّخْرُفِ
attested.says: Ibn ʿAbbās: it came down in Makkah. Recorded by Ibn Mardawayh.

setting: The objection this surah answers is one of the most revealing the idolaters ever made. They did not say that the Qurʾan was false. They said it had come to the wrong person. “Why was this Qurʾan not sent down to a great man from one of the two towns?” — the two towns being Makkah and Ṭāʾif, and the great men, in the commentators’ reports, al-Walīd ibn al-Mughīrah of the one and ʿUrwah ibn Masʿūd of the other. Muḥammad ﷺ was an orphan of modest means. A message from the Lord of the worlds, they felt, should have gone to money.

“Is it they who portion out the mercy of your Lord?” the surah asks. It is We who have portioned out their livelihood among them in this life — and the mercy of your Lord is better than what they amass. Then the passage that gives the surah its name: silver roofs, silver stairways, doors, couches, and gold. All of that is nothing but the passing enjoyment of this life. Pharaoh is brought as the witness. His whole argument against Mūsā was this one: “Is not the kingdom of Egypt mine, and these rivers flowing beneath me? Am I not better than this man, who is contemptible and can hardly make himself clear? Why have bracelets of gold not been put upon him?”

The surah opens with the other inheritance Quraysh relied on: their fathers. “We found our fathers upon a way, and we are guided in their footsteps.” Against it stands the one forefather they were proudest of, Ibrāhīm, who told his father and his people: “I am free of what you worship — except Him who originated me.”

It also records an argument they thought they had won. When the Qurʾan said that what they worshipped besides Allah would be fuel for Hell, someone objected that the Christians worship ʿĪsā — so is he, too, in the Fire? Quraysh cried out in delight. The surah’s reply is that they were only being contentious: “He was nothing but a servant on whom We bestowed favour.” The Prophet ﷺ said of this: no people go astray after guidance except that they are given to disputation.

occasions.title: “Are our gods better, or is he?”
occasions.text: When the son of Maryam was put forward as an example, Quraysh raised a clamour, saying, “Are our gods better, or is he?” The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “No people have gone astray after being upon guidance but that they were given to argument.” Then he recited: “They put it to you only for argument’s sake. No — they are a contentious people.”
occasions.source: Abū Umāmah: al-Tirmidhī (3253), who graded it ḥasan ṣaḥīḥ; ḥasan according to al-Albānī.

aim: To set out the true principles of the Qurʾan, and to demolish the false notions of the Age of Ignorance.

outline.title: The Book, and the favours they ride on
outline.summary: Ḥā Mīm. By the clear Book: We have made it an Arabic Qurʾan, that you may understand; and it is in the Mother of the Book, with Us, exalted and wise. If you ask them who created the heavens and the earth, they will say, “The Almighty, the All-Knowing created them.” He made for you ships and animals to ride, that you may settle on their backs and say: “Glory be to Him who has subjected this to us; we could not have done it ourselves. And to our Lord we shall return.”

outline.title: Daughters, and fathers
outline.summary: Yet they assign to Him a portion of His servants. Has He taken daughters from what He creates, and favoured you with sons — when, if one of them is given news of a daughter, his face darkens? They have made the angels, who are servants of the Most Merciful, into females. They say: “We found our fathers upon a way, and we follow in their footsteps.” So it was said by the affluent of every town to which a warner was sent.

outline.title: Who portions out mercy?
outline.summary: Ibrāhīm said to his father and his people: “I am free of what you worship, except Him who originated me.” They say: “Why was this Qurʾan not sent down to a great man from the two towns?” Is it they who distribute the mercy of your Lord? Were it not that mankind would become one community, We would have given those who disbelieve in the Most Merciful roofs of silver for their houses, and stairways, doors and couches — and ornaments of gold. All that is only the enjoyment of this life; and the Hereafter, with your Lord, is for the mindful.

outline.title: A companion from among the devils
outline.summary: Whoever is blind to the remembrance of the Most Merciful, We assign him a devil as his companion — until, when he comes to Us, he says: “If only there were between me and you the distance of the two easts.” So hold fast to what has been revealed to you: you are upon a straight path. It is a reminder for you and your people, and you will be questioned.

outline.title: Pharaoh’s boast
outline.summary: We sent Mūsā with Our signs to Pharaoh and his chiefs, and they laughed at them. Pharaoh proclaimed among his people: “Is not the kingdom of Egypt mine, and these rivers flowing beneath me? Am I not better than this contemptible man? Why have bracelets of gold not been cast upon him, or angels come with him?” He made fools of his people, and they obeyed him. When they angered Us, We took retribution and drowned them all.

outline.title: The son of Maryam
outline.summary: When the son of Maryam was cited as an example, your people cried out at it. He was only a servant whom We favoured, and made an example for the Children of Israel. And he is a sign of the Hour; so do not doubt it. ʿĪsā said: “Allah is my Lord and your Lord, so worship Him: this is a straight path.” But the factions differed among themselves. Close friends, that Day, will be enemies to one another — except the mindful.

outline.title: The two abodes
outline.summary: “My servants, there is no fear upon you today, nor shall you grieve. Enter the Garden, you and your spouses, in joy.” Dishes and cups of gold are passed among them; there is whatever souls desire and eyes delight in. The guilty are in the punishment of Hell, abiding: they call out, “O Mālik, let your Lord make an end of us.” He will say: “You will remain.”

outline.title: The Lord of the Throne
outline.summary: Say: if the Most Merciful had a son, I would be the first to worship. Glory to the Lord of the heavens and the earth, Lord of the Throne, above what they describe. It is He who is God in the heaven and God on the earth. And his saying: “My Lord, these are a people who do not believe.” So turn from them and say, “Peace”; they will come to know.

keyAyah.why: The answer to every claim that standing with Allah follows standing among people: it is He who divides livelihoods, and His mercy is better than what they gather.

virtues.text: When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ had settled on his camel to set out on a journey he would say “Allāhu akbar” three times, and then: “Glory be to Him who has subjected this to us; we could not have done it ourselves. And to our Lord we shall surely return.”
virtues.arabic: سُبْحَانَ الَّذِي سَخَّرَ لَنَا هَذَا وَمَا كُنَّا لَهُ مُقْرِنِينَ وَإِنَّا إِلَى رَبِّنَا لَمُنْقَلِبُونَ

virtues.text: “No people have gone astray after the guidance they were upon, except that they were given to disputation.” Then he recited: “They put it to you only for argument’s sake; rather, they are a contentious people.”

before: Al-Shūrā ended with revelation described as a light by which Allah guides whom He wills. Al-Zukhruf answers those who thought they knew whom He ought to have willed.
after: Al-Zukhruf ends: turn from them and say, “Peace” — they will come to know. Al-Dukhān tells what they will come to know.
